title: Tasks contract
description: The ai.nimblebrain.tasks contract: its identity, version, cardinality, whether it needs run grants, its tools with their visibility, unattended marking and schemas, and the closed list of errors. Every tool error is a tools/call result with isError: true whose first text content is JSON {code, error}. A private tool's code is from errors.private. A public tool's code, and the answer to a tool name the server does not have, is from errors.public, and its error begins with that entry's prefix. Beyond the prefix, error is diagnostic. A request refused before any tool runs is the transport's answer and outside this list. Normative rules: contracts/tasks/CONTRACT.md in the NimbleBrain repository.

public.meaning: The taskId names no task in the caller's scope: another owner's, another workspace's and a missing one answer alike.
create named a task whose id is already stored in scope. Nothing was written.
The runId names no run in the caller's scope.
The batchId names no batch in the caller's scope.
The call contradicts what is stored: an idempotencyKey repeated with another definition, a batch action its state refuses, a budget at or below what is spent. Nothing was written.
A call that stores a definition (create, or run or run_batch with a definition) carried no grant in its host context. Nothing was written.

public.prefix: Not available in an unattended run:
public.meaning: A tool marked unattended "refused" was called with unattended: true in its host context. Nothing was read or written.
tools/call reached a public tool with no workspace or no authenticated identity in its scope.

The arguments do not match the tool's input schema, or a rule the schema cannot state (an unknown timezone, a cron that does not parse, an input that fails the task's inputSchema); the tool name follows the prefix, quoted. Nothing was written.
No tool by that name, public or private.

private.meaning: A private tool was called by a principal other than host. Checked before the input and the scope, so the answer reveals nothing about either. Nothing was read or written.
The arguments do not match the tool's input schema. Nothing was written.
The call reached the server with no workspace in its scope, or (begin_run, end_run, check_runs, offer_event) no owner. Nothing was read or written.
begin_run or end_run carried a token lower than one already recorded for that run: a newer claim holds it. Nothing was written.
end_run named a run that begin_run never answered with a work spec in scope.
offer_event named a task absent from the caller's scope.
Anything else. The error text is diagnostic only.

manifest.description: Task definition: identity, schedule, run-time policy.

schedule.description: Exactly one of `cron`, `at`, `intervalMs`, or `match`. Omit to run only on demand.

cron.description: Recurs on a 5-field cron expression (`0 7 * * 1-5`), read in `timezone`.

at.description: Fires once at this ISO-8601 time (with an offset).

intervalMs.description: Recurs every this many ms. Min 60000.

match.description: Fires on matching notifications routed to this task by an admin.

source.description: Exact connector server name. Omit to match every source in this workspace.

name.description: Glob over the event name the server chose, e.g. `domain.*`. Omit to match every name.

level.description: Minimum level, not an exact match.

timezone.description: IANA timezone for `cron`. Default: the implementation's.

debounceMs.description: With `match`: ms that matching notifications coalesce into one run. Default 30000.

maxFiresPerHour.description: With `match`: max runs per hour before the task disables. Default 12.

enabled.description: Whether its schedule fires. Default true.

kind.description: `saved` (default), or `oneoff` for a task run once: hidden from list and deleted after the retention window.

skills.description: Skills each run is given in full, by name.

model.description: provider:model-id or a slot name (fast). Omit for the workspace default.

thinkingEffort.description: Reasoning depth for its runs. Omit for the workspace setting.

allowedTools.description: Tools its runs may use: one `<connector>__*` glob per connector. Omit for every tool.

maxIterations.description: Max model iterations per run. Default 25.

maxInputTokens.description: Input tokens one run may spend. Omit for no cap.

maxRunDurationMs.description: Max wall-clock per run, in ms. Default 120000.

tokenBudget.description: Token limit across runs. Spent, the task is disabled.

maxInputTokens.description: Input tokens its runs may use per period.

maxOutputTokens.description: Output tokens its runs may use per period.

period.description: `daily` or `monthly` reset. Omit for a lifetime total.

inputSchema.description: JSON Schema each run's `input` must match.

outputSchema.description: JSON Schema the deliverable must match.

onPoorResult.description: What a deliverable that fails the outputSchema does: record, notify (default), or retry_once.

body.description: The prompt every run starts from: the job, and where to deliver its result.

timezone.description: The IANA timezone its schedule is read in: the schedule's own, else the implementation's.

taskId.description: The task's id, as list returns it.

idempotencyKey.description: Repeat-safe key. A later call with the same key returns what the first call started instead of starting another. With an inline definition, a repeat must give the same definition.

runId.description: The run's id, as run, runs, or upcoming return it.

taskId.description: The run's task. Needed only for a run past the newest 1000 of its task; any other is found by its id alone.

uri.description: Opaque: the host's reference to the file.

label.description: Only runs that ended reading as this label. Runs still queued or running are in upcoming.

verdict.description: Only runs with this verdict. A run with no deliverable has none, and never matches.

since.description: ISO timestamp — only runs started on or after this time.

before.description: ISO timestamp — only runs started before this time. Pages back through the run history: pass the previous response's `nextBefore`, with or without `taskId`.

excludeBatchRuns.description: true: leave out runs that are items of a batch (read those with batch).

runId.description: The run's id, as run, runs, or upcoming return it.

days.description: How many days ahead to list scheduled fires. Default 7, max 30. Every enabled timed task's next fire is listed even when it falls past the window.

since.description: ISO timestamp: count runs started on or after it. Default: 30 days ago.

taskId.description: Only this task (any kind). Default: every saved task.

name.description: What to call it in the Runs list. Display only: it names no task and is not part of what an idempotencyKey compares.

body.description: The prompt that opens each run (as create's body). Omit only with `manifest.skills`.

items.description: The inputs, one run each (at most 10,000; each at most 64 KiB serialized, 16 MiB together). Every item is checked against the task's inputSchema first: if any fails, the whole batch is refused (naming the first bad indices) and nothing is created.
One run's JSON input, checked against the task's inputSchema.

concurrency.description: Most of the batch's runs at once (queued or running). The host's fair share between workspaces applies on top.

budgetUsd.description: Whole-batch ceiling in USD, checked before every model call across all of the batch's runs at once. When what is left cannot pay for another item, no new item starts and the batch pauses (resume with a higher `budgetUsd`). An item that costs more than what is left can grant one run ends with errorCode exceeds_share and the batch goes on (rerun_failed with a higher `budgetUsd` runs it again).

stopWhen.description: Pause the batch when its pass rate collapses. Needs a task with an outputSchema.

minPassRate.description: Pause when pass / (pass + fail) falls below this (0..1).

afterItems.description: Assessed runs before the rule applies.

idempotencyKey.description: Repeat-safe key. A later call with the same key returns what the first call started instead of starting another. With an inline definition, a repeat must give the same definition.

results.description: true: include item results, a page at a time. A filter, cursor, or limit also asks for them.

filter.description: Only items in this state: a verdict (pass, fail, uncertain, not_assessed), an execution without a deliverable (failed, skipped, cancelled), pending (not ended), or failing (fail or failed).

cursor.description: Item index to start the page at: the previous page's `nextCursor`.

output.description: What each result row carries of its run's structured output. summary (default): its top-level scalar fields. full: the whole structured output as `structured`; a page then also ends when its rows reach a size budget, so follow `nextCursor`.

action.description: pause: no new item starts; runs still queued are taken back, runs in flight finish. resume: start items again. cancel: stop for good, cancelling queued and running runs. rerun_failed: run again, each as a new run, every item that failed, was skipped or cancelled, was judged fail, or ended with errorCode exceeds_share.

budgetUsd.description: With resume or rerun_failed of a batch that is not running: the budget to run under (more than already spent). A running batch refuses it (pause first).

until.description: List occurrences due at or before this instant.

ownerId.description: The owner the run acts for. The host runs it as this owner, in this workspace.

key.description: Names the occurrence within the workspace: the host enqueues it under this key, so a repeat of the same occurrence is one item. Stable for as long as the occurrence is due.

ref.description: What begin_run is called with when the occurrence is claimed.

notBefore.description: Not due before this instant. Absent: due at once (a requested run).

ref.description: The occurrence's ref, as due listed it.

attempt.description: The claim's attempt: above 1, an earlier claim may have begun the run.

token.description: The claim's fencing token, greater than every earlier claim's.

now.description: The host's now: what lateness, budgets and backoff are judged against.

runId.description: The run's id, minted by the implementation.

grant.description: The run grant the implementation stored with the definition, returned verbatim. The host verifies it before admitting the run.

prompt.description: The instruction that opens the run. Empty only with `skills`: the run then carries the skills out.

input.description: The run's JSON input, at most 65536 bytes serialized. Data, never instructions: the host contains it.

notes.description: Context the implementation adds to this run (an event's items, a retry's reason). Contained like `input`.

outputSchema.description: The JSON Schema the deliverable must match. The host renders the instruction.

allowedTools.description: Tools its runs may use: one `<connector>__*` glob per connector. Omit for every tool.

skills.description: Skills each run is given in full, by name.

limits.description: The definition's caps. The host lowers each to its own ceiling.

maxIterations.description: Max model iterations per run. Default 25.

maxInputTokens.description: Input tokens one run may spend. Omit for no cap.

maxRunDurationMs.description: Max wall-clock per run, in ms. Default 120000.

model.description: provider:model-id or a slot name (fast). Omit for the workspace default.

thinkingEffort.description: Reasoning depth for its runs. Omit for the workspace setting.

id.description: Opaque. Runs naming the same id share one balance while any of them is in flight.

remaining.description: What is left, in `unit`. Read only from the first run in flight to name `id`.

sharedBy.description: The most runs that may draw on it at once (a batch's concurrency).

exclusiveKey.description: At most one run per key is in flight in the workspace. The host refuses a run whose key is taken (outcome not_started, exclusive_busy).

trigger.description: What woke the run, for the host's telemetry. Decides nothing.

runId.description: The run's id, minted by the implementation.

token.description: The token begin_run was called with.

startedAt.description: When the run started, or was refused when it never started.

output.description: The deliverable: the final answer's text. Empty when none.

stopReason.description: Why the run stopped. not_started: refused before its first model call (see `error`).

wrapUpLimit.description: With stopReason complete: the limit that made the host tell the run to finish, which it did. Its answer may leave work undone.

transient.description: Whether the same run may succeed later unchanged (an outage, a rate limit).

message.description: Diagnostic, fit to show the owner.

unpricedCalls.description: Model calls with no known rates, not in costUsd.

spendAccountId.description: With stopReason spend_limit: the account that stopped it, one the spec named or one the host holds (an id the implementation did not name).

limits.description: The caps the run executed under, after the host's ceilings.

name.description: The tool's name as the model called it.

errorReason.description: Why it failed, when the tool or the host said (`bad_input`, …).

held.description: It did not run: it waited for its tool's guidance.

filesWritten.description: Files the run wrote, as the host recorded them.

id.description: Stable for the event it reports, so a repeated end_run delivers it once.

link.description: A resource the notice opens (the implementation's screen).

runIds.description: Runs of this workspace the host has in flight.

items.description: The run's id, minted by the implementation.

stop.description: Those to stop now (cancelled). Each ends with stopReason cancelled.

id.description: Unique per source; delivery is at least once, so a repeat is the same event.

now.description: The host's now: what debounce and the fire ceiling are judged against.

outcome.description: skipped: a condition that clears on its own (the task is off, or did not ask for it). denied: a configuration refusal only a person changes.

reason.description: One line an operator can act on.

endedBefore.description: Remove what ended before this instant.
